nodes.text: Come in quietly, if you would. The tinctures settle better in a calm room. I'm Wyn. Wounds, weariness, and everything the mountain does to lowland lungs: somewhere on these shelves is the answer.

choices.text: You trade with the Last Lamp?

nodes.text: More than the lowlands credit. Ledge-flowers that bloom late and hold long. Sagewort gone small and fierce with the altitude. Half the dose does twice the work, mind that if you buy it. And snow-moss the rams won't touch, which is how you know it's medicine.

A crate of tinctures down to Edda's lamp every season, since before the trade had my name on it. She sends back the empties and a note that says the same thing every year: 'still alive, no thanks needed, the amber one wants more bite.' From Edda, that counts as fondness. Her sister keeps our shrine. The stubbornness runs in the family.
Green for wounds, amber for weariness, and the salve for everything the road rubs raw.
